content.title: About
content.content: Potato french fries are deep‑fried strips or sticks of potato. They are a popular side dish and snack in restaurants and fast‑food outlets worldwide. When prepared correctly, they offer a fragrant taste, a crispy exterior, and a soft interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first documented french fry recipe appeared in France in the late 19th century.
In the United States, fries are commonly served with ketchup, mayo, or sweet chili sauce.
There are more than 30 cutting styles: classic sticks, crinkle‑cut, shoestring, waffle, and curly fries.
French fries are often featured in culinary competitions for their golden color and crunch.
In some countries, such as Belgium, the best fries are believed to be double‑fried.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which helps maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: When cooked properly, potatoes retain vitamin C, an antioxidant that supports immune health.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates in potatoes provide a quick source of energy.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The skin contains fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Yellow and orange potatoes contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories; portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Reusing oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salting can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, typically with dipping sauces such as ketchup, mayo, or cheese sauce. Sprinkle with seasonings like paprika, garlic, or rosemary. In restaurants they are often presented in portion boxes or paper bags.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked fries are best eaten immediately. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat in an oven to restore crispness.
